candidate.answerReason: The parallel lines give equal areas for triangles PCM and PCD. Subtracting these from triangle BPC shows [BPD]=[BMC], which is half of [ABC] because M is the midpoint of AB.

methods.label: Subtract equal areas
methods.explanation:
Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). The parallel condition gives an area equality without requiring any lengths. Triangles \(PCM\) and \(PCD\) share the base \(PC\), and their other vertices \(M\) and \(D\) lie on the line \(MD\), parallel to \(PC\). Their heights are therefore equal, so
\[
[PCM]=[PCD].
\]
The order on \(AB\) is \(A,P,M,B\). In triangle \(BPC\), the segment \(MC\) separates off triangle \(PCM\), while \(PD\) separates off triangle \(PCD\). Hence
\[
[BMC]=[BPC]-[PCM]
\]
and
\[
[BPD]=[BPC]-[PCD].
\]
Subtracting equal areas from the same triangle gives \([BPD]=[BMC]\).

Finally, \(CM\) is a median of \(ABC\). Triangles \(AMC\) and \(BMC\) have equal bases \(AM=MB\) and the same height from \(C\), so each has half the area of \(ABC\). Thus
\[
r=\frac{[BPD]}{[ABC]}=\boxed{\frac12},
\]
independent of the allowed position of \(P\). The answer is choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses equal-base equal-height triangle areas, subtraction of areas, and the midpoint condition.

methods.label: Use similarity and common heights
methods.explanation:
Write \([XYZ]\) for triangle area. Since \(P\) is between \(A\) and \(M\), the point \(M\) lies between \(B\) and \(P\). In triangle \(BPC\), the parallel \(MD\parallel PC\) makes triangles \(BMD\) and \(BPC\) similar by their equal angles. Their corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{BD}{BC}=\frac{BM}{BP}.
\]
We can connect these side ratios to areas by choosing common heights. Triangles \(BPD\) and \(BPC\) have bases \(BD\) and \(BC\) on the same line and share the height from \(P\), so
\[
\frac{[BPD]}{[BPC]}=\frac{BD}{BC}.
\]
Triangles \(BPC\) and \(ABC\) share the height from \(C\) to \(AB\), giving
\[
\frac{[BPC]}{[ABC]}=\frac{BP}{BA}.
\]
Multiplying and using similarity, with all lengths positive, yields
\[
r=\frac{BM}{BP}\cdot\frac{BP}{BA}
=\frac{BM}{BA}=\boxed{\frac12}.
\]
The dependence on \(P\) cancels, so the answer is choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary triangle similarity and area ratios justified by shared heights.
